question.problem: Solve the inequality $5x+13 \ge 3x-7$ and sketch the solution on the number line.
question.worked_solution:
We solve the inequality just like we would solve an equation.

First, we apply the addition principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+13 & \ge 3x-7 \\ 5x+13-3x & \ge 3x-7-3x \\ 2x+13 & \ge -7 \\ 2x+13-13 & \ge -7-13 \\ 2x & \ge -20\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the multiplication principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & \ge -20 \\ \frac{2x}{2} & \ge \frac{-20}{2} \\ x & \ge -10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x \ge -10.$

Our solution can be expressed using a number line, as shown below.
